distractors.reason: 'Very' modifies gradable adjectives (very big), not past participles used as passive adjectives. 'Very adopted' sounds unnatural.
'Deeply' expresses intensity of feeling (deeply concerned), not how far something has spread. 'Deeply adopted' is not used.
'Totally' means completely. Adoption is measured by how far something has spread, so 'totally adopted' is unnatural.

example_sentence: Remote collaboration software is now ___ adopted by most companies.
l1_interference: Los hispanohablantes a veces traducen 'muy' literalmente como 'very' y dicen 'very adopted'. Con participios en inglés se usa 'widely' (ampliamente), no 'very'.
explanation: In English, 'widely' is used with past participles to describe how far something has spread among people or places. Think of it as measuring the reach of something, not its intensity.

related_collocations.example: Smartphones are now widely used around the world.
Automation is widely accepted in modern factories.
High-speed internet is widely available in cities.

memory_tip: WIDELY = spread across many people or places (widely adopted, widely used) | VERY = intensity before gradable adjectives (very fast, very big)
